kind: first-hand published account by the collector himself
title: A Journey to the Tea Countries of China; including Sung-Lo and the Bohea Hills; with a short notice of the East India Company's tea plantations in the Himalaya Mountains
creator: Robert Fortune
origin: Robert Fortune, agent of the East India Company Court of Directors
interest: Gains reputation and book sales from a successful, adventurous mission; his own counts (20,000 plants) are self-reported, not audited. He also had an interest in praising the China plants over the Assam establishment.

kind: official correspondence of the Committee of Tea Culture and its frontier officers, printed by the society journal
title: IV. Discovery of the Genuine Tea Plant in Upper Assam, Journal of the Asiatic Society of Bengal vol. 4 (Jan 1835), pp. 42-49
creator: Committee of Tea Culture (Calcutta), Capt. F. Jenkins, Lieut. A. Charlton; editor's note citing Capt. Wilcox
interest: The Committee and the officers gained credit for a 'discovery' that justified a Company tea industry; they had reason to stress that the plant was genuine and inside Company territory. OCR garbles names (Jenxins, Caartron).
